chapter: Pianists, Basie, Lil Armstrong and closing
title: Tiny Parham's big band at the Savoy
summary: Saunders worked with Tiny Parham in the mid-1930s; Parham was mostly an arranger who wrote for shows and played a gig band two nights a week.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: You mentioned in one of your earlier interviews that you had worked some with Tiny PARHAM.
He's sort of a mystery figure in the history of jazz.

Yeah, right, he -- I didn't know -- I don't know too much about his history. I worked with him in the Savoy Ballroom. We played the Savoy Ballroom, and then the Savoy Ballroom was on the decline. And then I left out of there and then I went to the Club Delisa. But Tiny --

Yeah, right. And then Tiny was -- well, he was a great big guy, and he played piano. I don't guess he played -- his long suit was arranging, and he used to write for shows. And he wrote for Colossimo's (PHONETIC). This was down with -- when the Colossimo's was down on Wabash?

Yes, right, right down there, I mean, -- yeah, Royal Frolics, I think, was the name of the club, because at one time they turned -- then they brought Billie Holiday in there later. But later years. But he and Sammy Dyer -- Sammy Dyer was a great choreographer here who did shows for the Club Delisa. Also, he did the -- he did a lot of work for Mrs. Abbott with the Abbott girls in the Palmer House, yeah, when they had the Empire Room, first started out they started out with this great big line of girls and things, and Sammy used to teach them, too.
And Tiny used to do a lot of writing them.
What kind of band did he have at the Savoy?
Well, we had a swing, then, the swing era.
Yeah, it was a big band, right. And we had -- the personnel kind of fluctuated because it was more or less like a gig band. We were working there maybe two
nights a week, Friday and on Sunday or something like that. Personnel would change to different --
How did he play? He played piano, didn't he?
Yeah, he played, but he wasn't too much of a -- soloist.
